Folks —

I reviewed BrightScale's redlines and drafted counter-language; key points below:

1) Auto-renew notice window
Proposed: "Either party may elect not to renew by providing written notice at least seventy-five (75) days prior to the end of the then-current Term."
Rationale: 75 days preserves operational lead time for contract closeout and provisioning changes while moving toward BrightScale's ask.

2) Termination for Convenience (mutual)
Proposed: "Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon at least sixty (60) days' prior written notice. If Customer terminates for convenience, Redwood will: (a) refund any pre-paid, unused fees on a pro rata basis for unused subscription months; and (b) for Customers with committed discounts, refund shall be adjusted to reflect amounts actually invoiced less previously provided volume discounts reasonably allocable to the unused portion. Termination by Redwood for convenience will provide Customer a pro rata refund for pre-paid unused periods. Parties agree to cooperate on an orderly offboarding plan, which may include temporary transition services governed by a separate SOW."
Rationale: The language ties refunds to invoiced amounts and protects Redwood from retrospective discount clawbacks; includes operational cooperation.

3) Pilot carve-out
Proposed: Add into the Order Form: "Pilot or trial SKUs explicitly listed on the Order Form shall not be considered a renewal-triggering Commitment and shall terminate at the pilot end date without automatic renewal unless otherwise specified in a subsequent Order Form."

Action items:
- Chloe: please confirm whether 75 days is acceptable to present to BrightScale (I think it will be perceived as a compromise).
- Kim: we need a brief billing example showing how the pro-rata refund and discount reconciliation would be calculated (line-item level) — can you produce a one-page example for the call?
- Laura: asking for executive authorization to present these counters and, if needed, sign a modest concession (75 days + pro-rata with wording above) to avoid losing momentum.
